steps.name: QC + DESeq2 DE, HFD vs chow
steps.question: Which genes differ between high-fat diet and chow in the 12 mouse liver samples (6 vs 6), and is sample_01 — library size ~4x below median — a distorting outlier or a benign low-depth sample?
steps.description: Load counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, mouse gene symbols, raw Salmon gene-level counts) and metadata.csv (condition column, 6 treated vs 6 control). QC: library sizes with sample_01 flagged, gene detection per sample, PCA/hierarchical clustering on variance-stabilised counts to check for latent structure beyond the single stated batch. Pre-filter genes with near-zero counts across all samples. Fit DESeq2 with design ~ condition (HFD vs chow), Wald test, BH FDR across all tested genes, and apeglm-shrunk log2 fold changes. Outputs: full DE results table, volcano plot, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, VST matrix, and an explicit verdict on sample_01 (its size factor, whether it clusters with its condition, and its influence on dispersion). Resources are modest: a 12,000 x 12 integer matrix fits easily in a few GB.
acceptance_criteria: DE results table covers every tested gene with baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj
Library-size and PCA plots produced; sample_01 depth discrepancy quantified numerically
DE gene counts reported at FDR < 0.05 and at FDR < 0.05 & |shrunken LFC| >= 1, separately for up and down
Verdict on sample_01 stated: retained or excluded for the primary call, with the reason

steps.name: Sensitivity DE excluding sample_01
steps.question: Do the HFD-vs-chow gene calls survive when the shallow sample (sample_01) is dropped, and which specific hits depend on it?
steps.description: Re-run the identical DESeq2 pipeline (same pre-filter, same design ~ condition) on the 11 remaining samples (5 vs 6, dropping whichever condition group contains sample_01). Reconcile the two fits: sign and shrunken-LFC concordance for all tested genes, Spearman correlation of Wald statistics, overlap and disagreement among DE gene sets (FDR < 0.05), and a per-gene sensitivity label on the union of hits: robust (significant in both), sample_01-dependent (significant only in one), or flipped direction. Output the second results table, an upset/venn comparison, and a reconciled gene table that downstream enrichment consumes.
acceptance_criteria: Second DE table for the 11-sample fit with the same columns as T1S1
Spearman correlation of statistics and count of direction flips reported
Union DE gene set labelled robust vs sample_01-dependent per gene
Reconciled table written with the same gene-key column as the counts matrix for downstream joins

steps.name: Hallmark + WikiPathways FGSEA
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are enriched among genes changing between HFD and chow, and do those pathway calls survive exclusion of sample_01?
steps.description: Run fgsea on the ranked DE statistics (Wald stat, ties broken by p-value) from T1S1 (primary) and T1S2 (sensitivity), against the staged MSigDB mouse hallmark gene sets (2026.1 MGI symbols GMT) as the primary collection and the staged WikiPathways Mus musculus GMT as a secondary, mechanism-level readout. First intersect the 12,000 count-matrix gene symbols with each GMT's member symbols and report the match rate and unmatched set sizes — low overlap means the enrichment is bounded by annotation, not biology. Limit gene-set size to 10-500, compute BH-adjusted pathway p-values, extract leading-edge genes per significant set, and produce a pathway-level comparison of full vs sample_01-excluded rankings (NES shift, significance flips). Report hallmark pathways up and down in HFD with direction, NES, padj, and their sensitivity label; if the mouse hallmark GMT or the WikiPathways GMT is absent at run time, run the collection that is present and state which is missing rather than substituting a human set.
acceptance_criteria: Symbol-overlap statistics between counts matrix and each GMT reported before enrichment
FGSEA results for hallmark with NES, pvalue, padj, size, and leading-edge genes per set
Primary (12-sample) and sensitivity (11-sample) enrichment tables compared; per-pathway sensitivity label assigned
Final report lists hallmark pathways with consistent direction in both fits, and flags any pathway significant in only one

plan.title: HFD vs chow liver DE + hallmark FGSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12,000 mouse gene-symbol counts x 12 liver samples (6 high-fat diet vs 6 chow, unpaired, single batch) plus a 12-row condition table, with one flagged sample (sample_01) whose library size sits ~4x below the median. The question — which genes and which hallmark pathways change — decomposes into (1) a rigorous two-group differential-expression analysis with QC that quantifies whether the shallow sample is a technical outlier or merely a low-depth outlier that DESeq2's size factors and negative-binomial model can absorb, (2) a sensitivity re-run excluding sample_01 so every DE call carries a 'depends on the shallow sample / does not' label, and (3) gene-set enrichment on the ranked DE statistics against the staged MSigDB mouse hallmark GMT (2026.1), with WikiPathways mouse as a secondary readout, run on both the full and the sample_01-excluded rankings so pathway conclusions inherit the same sensitivity label. DESeq2 is installed (R 1.52.0) and is the standard tool for raw Salmon gene-level counts of this size; apeglm-shrunk fold changes guard against the small-n inflation of unshrunken LFCs; fgsea (1.38.0) handles the 50-set hallmark collection in seconds.
